subject: Clarify data deletion window and training exclusion
messages:
From: Amira Shah <amira@skyboundhealth.com>
To: mateo_alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Clarify data deletion window & training exclusion

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the chat yesterday — the legal team asked me to follow up with a few concrete questions so we can sign off on the pilot PO. Can you clarify the following?

1) Deletion/erase window: after a customer requests deletion or terminates, what are the maximum timelines for: primary request processing, backups/restores, and any debug snapshots? We need worst-case numbers for contract language.

2) Backups & snapshots: do backups contain customer text, and are they ever used for model training or metrics? How long are backups retained?

3) KV cache & ephemeral stores: are any in-memory caches or logs ever persisted to long-term storage that could be used for model training?

4) "We do not train on your data": we need precise wording. Is this an absolute guarantee for all customers, or are there carve-outs (aggregated telemetry, opt-in research, synthetic derivations)? If there are carve-outs, what opt-in flows and controls exist?

5) Evidence/artifacts: can you provide an attestation or short document we can include in our vendor questionnaire? A short PDF with the retention timeline and the training exclusion statement would be ideal.

Appreciate a concise reply we can share with our privacy and procurement teams.

Best,
Amira Shah
Head of Legal Operations
Skybound Health

--
Amira Shah | amira@skyboundhealth.com

Hi Amira — thanks for the clear list. Looping in the retention/auth teams to make sure we give you precise contractual language (cc'd).

High-level answers up front:
- We do not use customer content (plain text, files, transcripts) to train or improve models by default. This is a standard enterprise assurance for Dedicated/Private deployments and for hosted customers that opt into the "no-train" pledge in their account settings or contract.
- Retention timelines vary by artifact type (live data, logs, backups, snapshots). I attached a brief process doc (DataDeletionProcess.pdf) with operational timings and the attestation template.

Internal next steps: Priyom/Mina — can you confirm worst-case timelines for backups and snapshots so I can send a finalized attestation to Amira? Also, please review the suggested wording in the attestation PDF and flag any carve-outs.

Amira — I'll send a short attestation PDF once operations confirms the windows. Can we assume Skybound prefers worst-case numbers in the contract (rather than average)?

Thanks,

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: mateo_alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>, mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 13:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Clarify data deletion window & training exclusion (technical details)

Quick technical breakdown to support the attestation: please treat these as worst-case upper bounds unless explicitly scoped otherwise in a Dedicated/Private contract.

1) Primary delete request (user/customer data surface):
- Standard flow: delete request submitted -> queued -> processed by data-ops job. Typical processing SLA: 24-72 hours. Worst-case (high load/complex replay): up to 7 days.

2) Debug snapshots & KV caches:
- KV cache: ephemeral in-memory or local GPU cache. Not persisted to long-term object storage by default. Any cache dumps used for debugging are isolated, access-controlled, and retained only for debugging windows; worst-case retention for debug snapshots is 30 days, but in exceptional escalations we may retain up to 60 days with explicit customer approval.

3) Backups and object-store snapshots:
- Backups are periodic snapshots for restore purposes. Backups can contain customer data. Retention policy: rolling backups retained for 90 days by default (worst-case), after which they are purged according to our retention job. Backups are not used to train models.

4) Aggregated telemetry / metrics:
- We may collect aggregated usage metrics (latency percentiles, token counts) that are non-identifiable. Aggregated telemetry is used for product improvement and capacity planning. It does not contain customer text.

5) "We do not train on your data" — precise language recommendation:
- Recommended contractual sentence: "Redwood Inference will not use Customer Content to train or improve foundation or service models, nor will Customer Content be incorporated into model training datasets, unless Customer expressly opts in via a documented and auditable process."
- Carve-outs to call out explicitly (if relevant): legal obligation to process data, anonymized aggregated metrics described above, and explicit customer opt-in for research programs.

6) Evidence / attestation artifacts:
- We can provide a signed attestation PDF (NoModelTrainingAttestation.pdf) and a short ops runbook extract. For customers requiring SOC/SIG questions answered, we provide tailored evidence packages.

7) Recommended contract appendix entries:
- Erase window (worst-case): primary deletion within 7 days; debug snapshots ephemeral <= 60 days w/approval; backups purged within 90 days; logs retained up to 180 days for security/audit unless otherwise agreed.

Links: internal deletion playbook (https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/DELETION-PLAYBOOK) — use this for fwd to customers if they request the runbook.

If we want to tighten any of the worst-case numbers for Skybound, we can offer a shortened SLA (e.g., 30-day backup purge) as a contract-level commitment for Dedicated or Private deployments.

— Priyom
Director, Data Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarify data deletion window & training exclusion

Hi Amira — thanks for the questions and the patience. Below is a concise summary you can paste into your vendor review; attaching a signed attestation as well.

Summary (contract-friendly):
- Training: Redwood Inference will not use Customer Content to train or improve foundation or service models, nor will Customer Content be included in model training datasets, unless Customer expressly opts in via a documented opt-in process. Aggregated, non-identifiable telemetry (e.g., latency percentiles, token counts) may be used for product improvement.
- Erase windows (worst-case upper bounds): primary deletion processed within 7 days; debug snapshots retained <= 60 days (only with explicit approval for debugging); rolling backups purged within 90 days; security/audit logs retained up to 180 days unless otherwise negotiated.
- Backups and snapshots: backups may contain customer content for restore purposes but are never used for model training. Any debug snapshot access is limited, logged, and time-bound.

Attachments: NoModelTrainingAttestation.pdf (signed) — this contains the attestation and the suggested clause for procurement legal.

Next steps: please confirm if you want the shorter SLA (e.g., 30-day backup purge) included in your PO; if so, I can have legal/ops generate an addendum and we can route it for signature.

Thanks and looking forward to getting Skybound onboarded.

Best,
Mateo
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachment: NoModelTrainingAttestation.pdf (signed by legal)
